name: Weather radar
description: Animated precipitation radar over a map, drawn on the server.

schema.name: location
schema.label: Location
schema.help: The map is centred here. Use Find, or type latitude,longitude.

schema.name: zoom
schema.label: Zoom
schema.help: 5 shows a large region, 10 a city. Radar detail stops improving above 7 (RainViewer) or 9 (US NEXRAD).

schema.name: frames
schema.label: Frames
schema.help: How many past radar images to animate. RainViewer has one every 10 minutes, US NEXRAD every 5 (at most 11).

schema.name: frame_ms
schema.label: Frame time (ms)
schema.help: How long each radar image stays up. The newest one is held longer.

schema.name: aspect
schema.label: Map shape
schema.help: Match the screen. Other shapes are cropped to fill it.

schema.name: darken_basemap
schema.label: Dark map
schema.help: A dimmed map makes the radar colours stand out.

schema.name: alerts
schema.label: Show weather alerts (US only)
schema.help: Active alerts for this point from the US National Weather Service.

settings.name: source
settings.label: Radar source
settings.help: RainViewer: past radar only, detail up to zoom 7. NEXRAD: United States only, free, no key.

settings.name: basemap_url
settings.label: Base map tile URL
settings.help: An https XYZ tile server with {z}/{x}/{y}. The OpenStreetMap servers are for light use only; heavy or commercial users should run or rent their own tile server.

attribution: Radar: RainViewer or Iowa Environmental Mesonet · Map © OpenStreetMap contributors
terms: RainViewer's free API gives past radar frames only and asks for attribution; check its current limits before commercial use. The Iowa Environmental Mesonet NEXRAD tiles cover the United States and are free to use. The default base map comes from tile.openstreetmap.org, which allows only light use under the OpenStreetMap tile usage policy and requires attribution: busy or commercial deployments should set their own tile server. Map tiles are kept for 30 days and radar frames are reused between refreshes. US alerts come from api.weather.gov (public domain).
